data.tesis_gestora: The Fund follows an active extension strategy on European equities, holding long positions of approximately 130% and short positions of approximately 30% of net assets via derivatives, while maintaining the same overall net market exposure as a traditional long-only portfolio. The investment process is bottom-up, fundamentally driven, supported by quantitative analysis. Goal: maximise alpha generation by buying securities considered attractive and selling short those considered less attractive. In Q1 2026 the Fund outperformed its benchmark MSCI Europe Index (Total Return Net) by 1.78pp (+0.83% vs -0.94%). Key contributors: stock selection and overweight in telecommunication services, and stock selection in materials. Key detractors: underweight in semiconductors & semiconductor equipment and stock selection in transportation. The team views the outlook for corporate profits as healthy in a normalised environment, supported by fiscal/monetary stimulus and the AI investment boom. Overweights: energy, banks, telecommunication services. Underweights: capital goods, food/beverage/tobacco, household/personal products. Morningstar Rating: 5 stars; Morningstar Medalist Rating: BRONZE; Category: Europe Large-Cap Blend Equity.
data.decisiones_tomadas: Largest sector increase: semiconductors & semiconductor equipment — ASML topped up following better-than-expected Q4 order numbers as the industry experiences tightness in memory chip supply. Largest sector decrease: pharmaceuticals, biotechnology & life sciences — the Swiss pharmaceutical company Roche Holding was sold from the portfolio as it continues to deliver high-profile trial disappointments and concerns surrounding its high R&D spend in the obesity category persist. Specific stock positioning during the quarter: maintained underweight in SAP (contributed positively after weak Q4 cloud backlog and Anthropic competition concerns); maintained overweight in SBM Offshore (contributed positively after strong 2025 revenue/EBITDA growth from three new FPSO start-ups); maintained not-holding stance on Eni (detracted after Eni beat expectations driven by new projects in Congo and Angola plus Venezuela gas-for-oil payments); maintained underweight in TotalEnergies (detracted after solid results including >$1bn oil trading profit and stock benefiting from Middle East tensions).
data.contexto_mercado: European markets began Q1 2026 strongly, extending late-2025 momentum on solid growth, upbeat earnings, firmer eurozone PMIs and easing inflation that kept the European Central Bank on hold. Sentiment then deteriorated, ending the quarter negatively as tariff uncertainty and conflict between the US and Iran weighed on risk appetite. March's volatility triggered a global sell-off amid higher inflation worries, driven by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz to most ships, impacting oil, LNG and fertiliser. Geopolitical escalation has begun to show up in activity data, with recent survey evidence pointing to weaker services momentum across major eurozone economies as uncertainty rises. Benchmark MSCI Europe TR Net returned -0.94% in the quarter.

citas_textuales.cita: While uncertainty remains over how the Middle East conflict will evolve, our base case scenario assumes near-term de-escalation, as many key players have strong incentives to reduce tensions and avoid further escalation.

In a normalised environment, the outlook for corporate profits is healthy, and revisions are trending higher in most regions and industries. Solid economic growth — fuelled by fiscal and monetary stimulus, and, of course, the artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom — is supportive of earnings.

The economic outlook for the eurozone is characterised by cautious optimism. Activity in continental Europe is expected to rise, driven in part by the substantial fiscal stimulus announced by Germany in 2025.

Policymakers are likely to remain willing to deploy targeted measures to cushion households and energy-intensive sectors when energy volatility spikes, which can help stabilise demand but may complicate inflation dynamics.
citas_textuales.contexto: Looking Ahead — policy response to energy volatility

data.outlook: Base case: near-term de-escalation in Middle East conflict. Healthy corporate profit outlook with positive earnings revisions across regions and industries, supported by fiscal/monetary stimulus and AI investment boom. Eurozone characterised by cautious optimism with activity expected to rise driven by Germany's 2025 fiscal stimulus. Risk to monitor: geopolitical escalation already showing up in weaker eurozone services PMIs.

posiciones_destacadas.motivo: Weaker-than-expected Q4 cloud backlog; macro uncertainty; Anthropic competition. Position contributed positively to Q1 performance.
2025 revenue and EBITDA growth exceeded expectations, driven by successful start-up of three large FPSO units. Contributed positively.
Decision detracted from performance — Eni beat expectations on new Congo/Angola production starts and Venezuela gas-for-oil cargo payments.

Decision detracted — TotalEnergies beat expectations with >$1bn oil trading profit, strong refining margins and new Brazil/US production starts; also benefited from Middle East-driven oil price rally.
Better-than-expected Q4 order numbers; industry experiencing tightness in memory chip supply. Largest sector increase was semiconductors & semiconductor equipment.
Continued high-profile trial disappointments; concerns over high R&D spend in obesity category. Largest sector decrease was pharmaceuticals, biotechnology & life sciences.
